Kalpataru Yashodhan is undoubtedly one of the finest residential societies in Andheri, offering an exceptional blend of comfort, community living, and prime location advantage. One of the standout aspects of Kalpataru Yashodhan is the vibrant community culture, with well-organised social events throughout the year that foster strong neighbourly bonds and create a warm, welcoming environment for families.

The amenities are thoughtfully designed to cater to all age groups. The swimming pool is spacious and well-maintained, perfect for both relaxation and fitness. The fully equipped gym allows residents to conveniently maintain an active lifestyle. Families with children particularly appreciate the safe and engaging kids’ play area, while the pickleball court adds a modern recreational touch that encourages social interaction and physical activity. The beautifully landscaped greenery within the premises provides a refreshing escape from the fast-paced city life and enhances the overall living experience.

Location is another major advantage. The society is within walking distance of Andheri station, making daily commuting extremely convenient. Additionally, it is surrounded by markets, essential stores, and several well-known eateries, ensuring everything one needs is easily accessible. Its prime location ensures excellent connectivity while still maintaining a peaceful residential atmosphere.

Overall, Kalpataru Yashodhan offers a perfect balance of lifestyle, convenience, and community, making it one of the most desirable places to live in Andheri.

For example, there were multiple instances where there have been broken rocks/floors/nets/equipment near children's playing area, and they take weeks and weeks to get it repaired (that too after multiple complaints), or not repair it at all. Multiple children and people get hurt or trip over broken tiles yet the repairs are not prioritised. There have also been broken equipment in the gym, and despite multiple complaints they were not fixed.

Another major issue I experienced is their cheap cost cutting methods. They only turn on the common area air conditioning for barely 2 hours in the evening. There are people literally sweating during other busy times throughout the day but they still keep them totally off. We didn't ask for you to keep them on 24x7 but surely more than 2 hours across multiple times in the day would've really left a good impression for residents and visitors. Every single other high-range apartments I visited the main thing and first impression was always the air conditioned common area.

All residents pay a fortune for monthly maintenance, and these aforementioned things should be the least to expect. It has been over a year since I left the apartments so I don't know if things have improved, but if they are, I look forward to seeing your reply and steps taken.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a really bad society. They are discriminatory in nature

A couple in Mumbai signed a rental agreement, paid the deposit, and completed police verification for a flat. However, when they arrived on the move-in day, the housing society refused to allow them into the building because the committee had not yet “approved” them. They were made to wait outside with their luggage, asked to return for a meeting the next day, and later kept waiting again while the society delayed the decision and hinted that the owner should apologise to them due to a prior disagreement. Frustrated and humiliated by the situation, the couple cancelled the agreement, the owner refunded them, and they ended up staying in a hotel while starting their house search again.
